# AOM-and-Bari-Surg-for-OSA-SRMA

## Purpose
Public Stata analysis repository and study-level extraction data for the systematic review, meta-analysis, and meta-regression of anti-obesity medications or bariatric surgery and apnea-hypopnea index in obstructive sleep apnea.

## Canonical identifiers
- Repository: https://github.com/reblocke/AOM-and-Bari-Surg-for-OSA-SRMA
- Final article DOI: https://doi.org/10.1111/obr.13697
- PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38342767/
- PubMed Central: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11311115/
- PROSPERO: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42022378853
- Baseline Stata release: https://github.com/reblocke/AOM-and-Bari-Surg-for-OSA-SRMA/releases/tag/stata-baseline-v1

## What is in this repository
- `OSA Wt Loss SRMA.do`: end-to-end Stata workflow for data processing, meta-analysis, meta-regression, sensitivity analyses, and figure generation.
- `Data Extraction Table.xlsx`: public study-level extraction workbook used by the Stata script.
- `ROB2_OSA SRMA.xlsx`: public risk-of-bias 2 assessment workbook.
- `README.md`: human-readable overview, citation, workflow, data access, and paper-code mapping.
- `CITATION.cff`: software citation and preferred article citation metadata.
- `data_dictionary.md` and `data_dictionary.csv`: machine-readable workbook headers, derived Stata variables, and generated-output documentation.
- `AGENTS.md`: repository-specific guidance for future coding agents.

## Data and license notes
The workbooks contain study-level extracted data and risk-of-bias assessments. They do not contain patient-level data or PHI. Code is MIT licensed. Reuse of the compiled study-level data should cite the Obesity Reviews article.

## Default run command
Run from the repository root:

```stata
do "OSA Wt Loss SRMA.do"
```

The script reads `Data Extraction Table.xlsx` from the repository root. It writes generated Stata datasets to `outputs/stata/` and generated figures, logs, and copied do-file snapshots to `Results and Figures/<date>/`.

## Agent cautions
- Preserve the legacy Stata analysis logic unless a future task explicitly asks for scientific refactoring.
- Do not copy publisher-formatted article text into the repository; link DOI, PubMed, PMC, and PROSPERO records instead.
- Keep README, `llms.txt`, `CITATION.cff`, `AGENTS.md`, and data dictionary files synchronized after article, release, workbook, or workflow changes.
- Validate `CITATION.cff` with CFF 1.2 tooling before publishing metadata changes.
